set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which feature separates papulopustular rosacea from acne vulgaris?
opts: Rosacea has no comedones
Correct — open or closed comedones point to acne vulgaris instead.
Rosacea produces pustules and acne vulgaris does not
Both produce pustules; the comedones are what differ.
Rosacea occurs only in patients over the age of sixty
Peak onset is between thirty and sixty.
Rosacea spares the central face entirely
Central facial involvement is characteristic of rosacea.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is used for suppressive therapy in recurrent herpes-associated erythema multiforme?
opts: Dapsone 25 to 200 mg daily with regular monitoring of the blood count
Dapsone is reserved for refractory recurrent disease that is not herpes-associated.
Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily taken indefinitely
Hydroxychloroquine is also reserved for refractory non-herpes recurrent disease.
Prednisone 40 to 60 mg daily for five days at each recurrence
A short steroid course is used in some acute settings rather than as suppression.
Acyclovir 400 mg twice daily or valacyclovir 500 mg daily
Correct. Dapsone or hydroxychloroquine are used for refractory non-herpes recurrent disease.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which systemic therapy has the strongest current evidence in toxic epidermal necrolysis?
opts: Prophylactic antibiotics covering skin and gut flora
Antibiotic prophylaxis is specifically not recommended.
Cyclosporine at 3 to 5 mg/kg daily, started early
Correct, with intravenous immunoglobulin and etanercept as adjunct options.
Intravenous immunoglobulin at 1 g/kg daily for three days
This is an adjunct option rather than the strongest evidence base.
High-dose systemic corticosteroids given for the first week
Corticosteroids remain controversial across the spectrum.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which investigation excludes phaeochromocytoma as a cause of secondary hyperhidrosis?
opts: Fasting glucose with haemoglobin A1c
Those assess diabetes, another secondary cause.
Twenty-four hour urine metanephrines and catecholamines
Correct — episodic sweating with headache, palpitations and hypertension is the clue.
Thyroid-stimulating hormone with anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies
Those assess thyroid disease, another secondary cause.
Serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation
That screens for monoclonal gammopathy in pyoderma gangrenosum.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which single feature most usefully distinguishes erythema nodosum from nodular vasculitis?
opts: Erythema nodosum nodules occur exclusively in men
There is a female predominance of three to six to one.
Erythema nodosum nodules do not ulcerate
Correct, and they sit on the anterior shins whereas nodular vasculitis favours the posterior legs and ulcerates.
Erythema nodosum nodules appear only on the posterior legs
The anterior shins are the characteristic site.
Erythema nodosum nodules are painless on palpation
The nodules are tender, which is part of the classic description.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which topical agent is the only one approved for photoaging, and how does it work?
opts: Niacinamide, which reduces inflammation and improves skin sallowness
Niacinamide is an adjunct rather than the approved agent.
Tretinoin, which stimulates collagen synthesis and inhibits matrix metalloproteinase activity
Correct, requiring a minimum of six to twelve months for visible results.
Hydroquinone, which inhibits melanin production within the epidermis
Hydroquinone treats hyperpigmentation but is not the approved photoaging agent.
Vitamin C, which neutralises reactive oxygen species and stimulates new collagen
Vitamin C is an adjunct antioxidant rather than the approved agent.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is the gold standard test for determining the cleavage plane in epidermolysis bullosa?
opts: Serum enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for structural protein antibodies
Inherited epidermolysis bullosa is not antibody-mediated.
Skin biopsy with transmission electron microscopy
Correct, with immunofluorescence antigen mapping used to localise missing or reduced proteins.
Skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence for immunoglobulin G
That distinguishes acquired autoimmune blistering disease rather than mapping the cleavage plane.
Genetic testing of the known structural protein genes
Genetic testing is confirmatory and guides prognosis and counselling.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which type of epidermolysis bullosa is most common, and what is its cleavage level?
opts: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa, at about 70% of cases, with cleavage in the lamina lucida
Junctional disease carries the highest mortality but is not the commonest.
Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, at about 70% of cases, with sub-lamina densa cleavage
Dystrophic disease arises from COL7A1 mutations but is not the commonest.
Kindler epidermolysis bullosa, at about 70% of cases, with mixed cleavage planes
Kindler disease is rare and arises from FERMT1 mutation.
Epidermolysis bullosa simplex, at about 70% of cases, with intraepidermal cleavage
Correct — it results from keratin 5 and 14 mutations and is autosomal dominant.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What distinguishes erythema multiforme minor from erythema multiforme major?
opts: Minor is drug-triggered; major is triggered by herpes simplex virus
Both forms share the same trigger list, with herpes simplex predominating.
Minor occurs in children; major occurs only in adults over forty
Peak occurrence for both is in adults aged twenty to forty.
Minor involves skin only; major involves two or more mucosal surfaces
Correct. Erythema multiforme minor constitutes the majority of cases.
Minor lasts under one week; major lasts more than one month
Lesions evolve over one to two weeks in both and the disease is self-limited.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which epidermolysis bullosa subtype carries the highest mortality?
opts: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex, especially the localised palmoplantar form
Simplex disease is localised to palms and soles and heals without scarring.
Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, especially the dominant form
Dystrophic disease causes severe scarring and squamous cell carcinoma risk rather than the highest mortality.
Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita, the autoimmune acquired form
This acquired form is autoimmune rather than genetic and is not the highest-mortality type.
Junctional epidermolysis bullosa, especially the Herlitz subtype
Correct, which is why early palliative care integration is appropriate in severe Herlitz disease.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which test is mandatory when investigating polymorphous light eruption?
opts: A porphyrin screen of urine, stool and red cells in every patient
That is done only if erythropoietic protoporphyria is suspected.
Photopatch testing with the standard photoallergen series
That is used when photoallergic contact dermatitis is suspected.
Skin biopsy, which shows a pathognomonic pattern
Biopsy is supportive rather than pathognomonic.
An antinuclear antibody panel, to exclude lupus erythematosus
Correct, especially anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which rosacea subtype is most common, and what defines it?
opts: Erythematotelangiectatic, with persistent central facial erythema, flushing and telangiectasias but no papules or pustules
Correct — the skin is often described as sensitive and stinging.
Papulopustular, with transient central facial papules and pustules on a background of erythema and no comedones
This is the classic presentation but not the most common subtype.
Phymatous, with skin thickening and nodular enlargement of the nose and chin
This predominates in males but is not the most common subtype.
Ocular, with blepharitis, conjunctivitis and meibomian gland dysfunction
This may precede or follow the skin findings but is not the most common subtype.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which biopsy finding is described as pathognomonic across the Stevens-Johnson and toxic epidermal necrolysis spectrum?
opts: Granular immunoglobulin A deposited within the dermal papillae of the skin
That is dermatitis herpetiformis.
Palisading granulomas surrounding an area of necrobiosis
That is granuloma annulare.
Septal panniculitis without any accompanying vasculitis
That is erythema nodosum.
Full-thickness epidermal necrosis with dermal-epidermal junction separation
Correct, on punch biopsy.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which pharmacogenomic association carries direct pre-prescription implications?
opts: HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8, for sulfonamide antibiotics
Those haplotypes relate to dermatitis herpetiformis and coeliac disease.
HLA-Cw6 in European populations, for aromatic anticonvulsants
That allele associates with early-onset psoriasis.
HLA-A31 and HLA-BW35, for nevirapine
Those are the suggested haplotypes for granuloma annulare.
HLA-B*15:02 in Asian populations, for carbamazepine
Correct, with HLA-B*58:01 associated with allopurinol.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which wavelength band is primarily responsible for sunburn, and by what mechanism?
opts: Ultraviolet A at 320 to 400 nm, causing direct DNA damage through pyrimidine dimers
Ultraviolet A contributes indirectly; ultraviolet B causes the direct damage.
Visible light at 400 to 700 nm, causing thermal injury to the epidermis
Sunburn is a photobiologic rather than a thermal injury.
Infrared radiation, causing collagen denaturation within the dermis
This is not the mechanism described.
Ultraviolet B at 290 to 320 nm, causing direct DNA damage through cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers
Correct, with ultraviolet A contributing through oxidative stress and indirect DNA damage.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which haplotypes are strongly associated with dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: HLA-Cw6 and HLA-B27
Those are associated with psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis.
HLA-A31 and HLA-BW35
Those are the suggested susceptibility haplotypes for granuloma annulare.
HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8
Correct, and nearly all patients have underlying gluten-sensitive enteropathy even when gastrointestinally asymptomatic.
HLA-B*15:02 and HLA-B*58:01
Those are the pharmacogenomic risk alleles for Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which drug classes are classic causes of phototoxicity?
opts: Aromatic anticonvulsants, allopurinol and nevirapine
Those are the leading triggers of Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
Oral contraceptives, sulfonamides and bromides
Those are drug triggers of erythema nodosum.
Tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, amiodarone and thiazides
Correct, alongside furosemide, voriconazole, some nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and psoralens.
Sunscreen chemicals, sulfonamides and phenothiazines
Those are the classic photoallergens rather than phototoxic agents.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which finding should prompt a search for hereditary angio-oedema?
opts: Recurrent angio-oedema occurring without any wheals
Correct — check complement C4 and C1-esterase inhibitor level and function.
Wheals that persist beyond twenty-four hours and leave bruising
That picture suggests urticarial vasculitis, investigated by biopsy.
Wheals accompanied by Darier's sign and an elevated tryptase
That combination suggests mastocytosis.
Wheals appearing only after exposure to cold or vibration
That indicates a physical urticaria rather than hereditary angio-oedema.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which biologic is approved for refractory chronic urticaria?
opts: Dupilumab, an interleukin-4 receptor antagonist given subcutaneously
Dupilumab has been reported in refractory granuloma annulare rather than approved here.
Etanercept, a tumour necrosis factor inhibitor given subcutaneously
Etanercept is described as an emerging adjunct in Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
Omalizumab, an anti-immunoglobulin E antibody given every four weeks
Correct, at 300 mg subcutaneously.
Infliximab, a tumour necrosis factor alpha inhibitor given intravenously
Infliximab is approved for pyoderma gangrenosum in inflammatory bowel disease.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is the hallmark histopathologic finding of dermatoheliosis?
opts: Solar elastosis, the replacement of normal collagen with thickened tangled elastin
Correct, alongside epidermal atrophy with loss of rete ridges and vascular ectasia.
Full-thickness epidermal necrosis with dermal-epidermal junction separation
That belongs to the Stevens-Johnson and toxic epidermal necrolysis spectrum.
Palisading granulomas with central mucin deposition
That belongs to granuloma annulare.
Interface dermatitis with vacuolar basal layer degeneration
That belongs to erythema multiforme.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What does the lecture say about patients with Fitzpatrick types IV to VI?
opts: They should use SPF 15 rather than SPF 30, on the basis that higher factors confer no additional benefit
The guidance is broad-spectrum SPF 30 or above for daily use across all types.
They are not immune to ultraviolet damage or skin cancer, and melanoma is frequently diagnosed at advanced stages
Correct — delayed diagnosis is common because of a lower index of suspicion.
They carry no meaningful skin cancer risk and need no routine photoprotection
Risk is lower but explicitly not absent.
They burn more readily than types I to III but tan more deeply afterwards
Types IV to VI burn minimally or never.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How is an isolated actinic keratosis usually treated?
opts: Cryotherapy with two to three freeze-thaw cycles
Correct — the standard of care for isolated lesions, with shave excision or curettage as alternatives.
5-fluorouracil cream applied for two to four weeks
That is a field-directed treatment for multiple or confluent lesions.
Imiquimod applied twice weekly for sixteen weeks
That is also field-directed rather than lesion-directed.
Photodynamic therapy using aminolevulinic acid and light
This is excellent for field treatment rather than an isolated lesion.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What does biopsy show in granuloma annulare?
opts: A dense neutrophilic infiltrate at the ulcer edge
That is pyoderma gangrenosum.
Interface dermatitis with scattered necrotic keratinocytes
That is erythema multiforme.
Palisading granulomas with central necrobiosis and mucin deposition
Correct — thought to involve a type IV delayed hypersensitivity reaction around degenerating collagen.
Septal panniculitis without vasculitis and Miescher's granulomas
That is erythema nodosum.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which systemic association is present in a quarter to a half of pyoderma gangrenosum cases?
opts: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
This is a recognised association but not the most frequent one.
Inflammatory bowel disease
Correct, and peristomal disease occurs in up to 15% of patients with intestinal ostomies and bowel disease.
Rheumatoid arthritis and seronegative arthritis
These are recognised associations but not at that frequency.
Haematologic malignancy such as acute myeloid leukaemia
This is associated particularly with the bullous variant but not at that rate.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How are acute and chronic urticaria distinguished, and how common is chronic disease?
opts: Acute lasts under six weeks; chronic exceeds six weeks and affects 0.5 to 1% of the population
Correct. Lifetime prevalence of urticaria overall is 15 to 25%.
Acute lasts under twenty-four hours; chronic exceeds twenty-four hours in any single lesion
That interval describes individual lesion duration, not the acute-chronic division.
Acute lasts under two weeks; chronic exceeds two weeks and affects 15 to 25% of people
Six weeks is the dividing line, and 15 to 25% is the lifetime prevalence of urticaria overall.
Acute is immunoglobulin E mediated; chronic is always autoimmune in origin
Over half of chronic urticaria is idiopathic rather than autoimmune.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which organism contributes to papulopustular rosacea?
opts: Demodex folliculorum, whose overgrowth drives inflammation
Correct, which is why ivermectin 1% cream outperforms metronidazole in Demodex-associated disease.
Malassezia, whose overgrowth drives inflammation in sebum-rich areas
Malassezia drives seborrhoeic dermatitis.
Staphylococcus aureus, colonising the follicles
This organism is not implicated in rosacea.
Cutibacterium acnes, proliferating within blocked follicles
That organism relates to acne vulgaris.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which test is the gold standard for diagnosing dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: Small bowel biopsy demonstrating villous atrophy consistent with coeliac disease
Up to 90% show villous atrophy, but that confirms coeliac disease rather than the skin diagnosis.
Perilesional skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence showing granular immunoglobulin A in the dermal papillae
Correct. Immunoglobulin A anti-epidermal transglutaminase is the most specific serological test.
Lesional skin biopsy with haematoxylin and eosin showing subepidermal blistering with neutrophils
Histology supports the diagnosis but the immunofluorescence pattern is what settles it.
Serum immunoglobulin A anti-tissue transglutaminase with anti-endomysial antibodies
These serologies support the diagnosis but are not the gold standard.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which single intervention most improves survival in Stevens-Johnson syndrome?
opts: Prophylactic broad-spectrum antibiotics started on admission
Antibiotic prophylaxis is explicitly not recommended; infections are treated when confirmed.
High-dose systemic corticosteroids given throughout the admission
Systemic corticosteroids remain controversial and are avoided in active infection.
Immediate withdrawal of the causative drug, since each day of delay worsens prognosis
Correct — earlier withdrawal is strongly associated with improved survival.
Early administration of intravenous immunoglobulin at 1 g/kg daily for three days
This shows benefit in retrospective studies but is not the intervention with the strongest survival link.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which counselling point is emphasised for acanthosis nigricans?
opts: It is a metabolic warning sign rather than a hygiene problem, and 5 to 10% weight loss improves the findings
Correct — the hygiene misconception is specifically addressed.
It is a benign cosmetic change that carries no systemic implication and requires no further investigation
It is a visible marker of insulin resistance and sometimes of malignancy.
It responds fully to topical antifungal therapy within several weeks
That would treat tinea versicolor, one of the differentials.
It resolves spontaneously in most patients without any intervention
It reflects an underlying process that must itself be treated.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which group carries markedly increased actinic keratosis risk?
opts: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease, at roughly 10 times the risk
That association belongs to pyoderma gangrenosum.
Patients with coeliac disease, at roughly 30 times the risk
That association belongs to dermatitis herpetiformis.
Organ transplant recipients, at roughly 65 times the risk
Correct, alongside Fitzpatrick types I and II, male sex, age over fifty and outdoor occupation.
Patients with atopic dermatitis, at roughly 20 times the risk
Atopy is not among the named risk factors.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which feature most reliably distinguishes primary from secondary hyperhidrosis?
opts: Primary disease always has an identifiable underlying cause
Primary hyperhidrosis is idiopathic; secondary disease has an underlying cause.
Primary disease is bilateral, focal and absent during sleep
Correct — secondary disease is generalised, may be asymmetric, and can occur at night.
Primary disease is generalised and worse at night
That pattern indicates secondary hyperhidrosis.
Primary disease begins after the age of fifty
Primary disease begins in adolescence, with peak onset between fourteen and twenty-five.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which biologic is approved for pyoderma gangrenosum in inflammatory bowel disease?
opts: Etanercept at 25 to 50 mg subcutaneously
That is described as an emerging adjunct in Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
Dupilumab given subcutaneously every two weeks
That has been reported in refractory granuloma annulare.
Infliximab at 5 mg/kg intravenously
Correct — the biologic of choice in that setting, with adalimumab and ustekinumab for refractory cases.
Omalizumab at 300 mg subcutaneously every four weeks
That is approved for refractory chronic urticaria.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the main differential for localised granuloma annulare, and how is it separated?
opts: Necrobiosis lipoidica, which has a yellow-waxy atrophic centre on the shins
This is a differential but is distinguished by its site and appearance rather than being the main one.
Rheumatoid nodules, which are firm, periarticular and serology positive
These are a differential chiefly for the subcutaneous variant.
Lichen planus, which is violaceous and polygonal with Wickham striae
This is a listed differential but not the principal one.
Tinea corporis, which has a scaling border and is potassium hydroxide positive
Correct — granuloma annulare has no scale on its ring.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How is the diagnosis of pyoderma gangrenosum established?
opts: By wound culture growing a characteristic organism
Cultures are obtained to exclude an infectious cause; they are negative in pyoderma gangrenosum.
By serum antibody testing against dermal structural proteins
The condition is not antibody-mediated in that way.
By exclusion, since there is no gold standard test
Correct — biopsy from the ulcer edge shows dense neutrophils and rules out malignancy and infection.
By biopsy showing a pathognomonic palisading granuloma
Palisading granulomas belong to granuloma annulare.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is pathergy, and what does it mean for management?
opts: Worsening of the ulcer with trauma or debridement, which is why debridement must be avoided
Correct — this is the single most consequential management point in the condition.
Spread of the ulcer to distant sites through the bloodstream
Pathergy refers to the local response to trauma rather than dissemination.
Failure of the ulcer to culture any organism despite clear clinical signs of infection
Culture negativity helps exclude infection but is not pathergy.
Recurrence of the ulcer at the same site after apparent healing
That describes a fixed recurrence rather than pathergy.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the hardening phenomenon in polymorphous light eruption?
opts: Loss of pigment in the affected areas after each episode
This is not a described feature.
Improvement through the summer as tolerance develops after repeated exposure
Correct, which is also why prophylactic narrowband ultraviolet B in spring is the most effective preventive strategy.
Thickening and hardening of the skin from repeated scratching of the eruption
That describes lichenification.
Progressive scarring of affected sites over successive seasons
The eruption resolves without scarring.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What mechanism underlies the most common form of acanthosis nigricans?
opts: Hyperinsulinaemia stimulating keratinocyte and fibroblast proliferation through insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor cross-activation
Correct — the insulin-resistant or benign form is the commonest.
A paraneoplastic process driven by an underlying gastric adenocarcinoma secreting growth factors that act on the epidermis
Malignant acanthosis nigricans is rare, at under 1% of cases.
A delayed type IV hypersensitivity reaction to a contacted allergen
That mechanism produces allergic contact dermatitis.
Autoantibody deposition along the epithelial basement membrane zone
That mechanism produces bullous pemphigoid.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the mortality of toxic epidermal necrolysis, and what predicts it at presentation?
opts: Under 1%, predicted by the number of drugs the patient was taking
Toxic epidermal necrolysis carries substantially higher mortality than this.
Around 50%, predicted by the presence of the Nikolsky sign
The Nikolsky sign is present across the spectrum and is not a prognostic score.
Up to 30 to 35%, predicted by the SCORTEN score calculated within 24 hours
Correct, and SCORTEN is repeated on day three.
Between 1 and 5%, predicted by the extent of mucosal involvement
That mortality figure belongs to Stevens-Johnson syndrome alone.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which investigation is used to look for the sarcoidosis association in erythema nodosum?
opts: Chest radiograph, seeking bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy
Correct — Löfgren syndrome, which has the best prognosis of all sarcoidosis presentations.
Colonoscopy, seeking mucosal ulceration and skip lesions
Colonoscopy is done when inflammatory bowel disease symptoms are present.
Antistreptolysin O titre with a throat culture
These exclude a streptococcal trigger.
Serum protein electrophoresis, seeking a monoclonal band
That screens for the gammopathy associated with pyoderma gangrenosum.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How is the classic erythema multiforme target lesion described?
opts: Grouped vesicles on an erythematous base following a single dermatome
That describes herpes zoster rather than erythema multiforme.
Three concentric zones: a central dusky or necrotic area, a pale oedematous ring, and an outer erythematous halo
Correct, and the lesions are distributed symmetrically on acral surfaces — palms, soles and dorsal hands.
Two concentric zones: a central pale area surrounded by a single wide erythematous ring
The classic lesion has three zones, not two, and the centre is dusky rather than pale.
A single uniform erythematous plaque with a raised advancing border and a clear centre, without any concentric zones
That describes an annular lesion such as tinea corporis rather than a target.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What distinguishes solar lentigo from lentigo maligna?
opts: Solar lentigo appears in early childhood; lentigo maligna appears only after the age of seventy
Solar lentigo reflects cumulative exposure, exceeding 90% prevalence in Caucasians over seventy.
Solar lentigo appears on covered skin; lentigo maligna on exposed skin
Solar lentigo occurs on chronically sun-exposed surfaces.
Solar lentigo has uniform pigmentation; lentigo maligna is asymmetric with irregular border and colour
Correct, and dermoscopy is essential — solar lentigo shows finger-like projections and a moth-eaten border.
Solar lentigo is raised and rough; lentigo maligna is flat and smooth
Solar lentigo is a macule without induration or scale.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What kind of process is erythema nodosum, histologically?
opts: A palisading granuloma around degenerating collagen
That describes granuloma annulare.
A dense neutrophilic infiltrate without organisms
That describes pyoderma gangrenosum.
A septal panniculitis without vasculitis
Correct — the most common form of panniculitis, a delayed hypersensitivity reaction in subcutaneous fat.
A lobular panniculitis with associated vasculitis
That describes nodular vasculitis, or erythema induratum, a differential.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the underlying mechanism of dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: Immunoglobulin G antibodies directed against the epithelial basement membrane zone of the skin
That mechanism produces bullous pemphigoid.
Immunoglobulin G antibodies against keratinocyte adhesion molecules
That mechanism produces pemphigus.
Immunoglobulin E mediated mast cell degranulation with histamine release
That mechanism produces urticaria.
Immunoglobulin A antibodies against epidermal transglutaminase, depositing in the dermal papillae
Correct, in genetically susceptible individuals consuming gluten, producing subepidermal blisters.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How much do tanning beds reduce risk compared with natural sun, and how are they classified?
opts: They are safer for Fitzpatrick types I and II under supervision
Those types carry the highest risk from any ultraviolet exposure.
They are acceptable if limited to the months outside peak summer
No safe level of tanning is described.
They are not safer at all, and are classified as Group 1 carcinogens
Correct — there is no safe level of tanning.
They halve ultraviolet B exposure while delivering the same ultraviolet A dose
No such reduction is described; they are classified as carcinogenic.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What causes phytophotodermatitis, and how does it present?
opts: A delayed hypersensitivity response to an ultraviolet-induced photoantigen
That describes polymorphous light eruption.
Furanocoumarins in plants such as lime, celery and parsley plus ultraviolet A, producing linear streaked hyperpigmentation
Correct — classically after lime juice and sun exposure, with painful blistering acutely.
Bergapten in bergamot oil used in fragrances and cosmetics, producing drip-pattern hyperpigmentation of the neck
That describes berloque dermatitis, a separate subtype.
A persistent eczematous eruption in chronically exposed skin of older males
That describes chronic actinic dermatitis.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which advice is given about blisters in second-degree sunburn?
opts: Do not pop them, because intact blisters are protective
Correct, with cool compresses and early nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for pain.
Drain them under sterile conditions to reduce infection risk
Intact blisters protect the underlying skin.
Apply a high-potency topical corticosteroid directly to them
Topical steroids have limited evidence and may help only within six hours.
Cover them with silver sulfadiazine to prevent colonisation
That agent is specifically avoided in severe cutaneous drug reactions.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How are Stevens-Johnson syndrome, the overlap state and toxic epidermal necrolysis separated?
opts: By the presence of mucosal involvement, which occurs only in the severe form
Mucosal erosions occur in over 90% of Stevens-Johnson syndrome and are nearly universal in toxic epidermal necrolysis.
By whether the trigger was a drug or an infection in each case
Both share the same causative agents, with drugs predominating.
By whether the Nikolsky sign is positive or negative at presentation
The Nikolsky sign is positive across the spectrum.
By body surface area of epidermal detachment: under 10%, 10 to 30%, and over 30%
Correct — the same disease spectrum divided by extent of detachment.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which surveillance is required in recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa?
opts: Annual squamous cell carcinoma surveillance after the age of ten
Correct — the severe scarring of dystrophic disease carries squamous cell carcinoma risk.
Annual colonoscopy from the age of ten to detect bowel involvement
Endoscopy is used if oesophageal stricture is suspected rather than for cancer surveillance.
Annual echocardiography to monitor for cardiomyopathy
This is not among the described surveillance requirements.
Annual bone density scanning to monitor for osteoporosis
This is not among the described surveillance requirements.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What distinguishes phototoxicity from photoallergy?
opts: Phototoxicity is immunologic and requires prior sensitisation before any reaction; photoallergy is non-immunologic, dose-dependent and occurs on the very first exposure
The mechanisms are reversed.
Phototoxicity affects only sun-exposed skin; photoallergy affects only covered skin
Photoallergy characteristically extends beyond sun-exposed skin.
Phototoxicity resolves on stopping the drug; photoallergy always resolves immediately too
Photoallergy can persist after the drug is stopped, as a persistent light reaction.
Phototoxicity is non-immunologic and dose-dependent and occurs on first exposure; photoallergy is immunologic and dose-independent and requires prior sensitisation
Correct — phototoxicity resembles an exaggerated sunburn within hours.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which variant of granuloma annulare carries the strongest systemic associations?
opts: Perforating, with central umbilication and extrusion of collagen
This variant may scar but is not the one with systemic associations.
Generalised or disseminated, associated with diabetes, thyroid disease, dyslipidaemia and lymphoma
Correct, and it is more common in adults over forty.
Localised disease, which predominates at about 75% of cases and affects children and young adults
Localised disease accounts for about 75% of cases and is asymptomatic.
Subcutaneous, occurring almost exclusively in children under six
This variant may mimic rheumatoid nodules but lacks those systemic links.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What does direct immunofluorescence show in erythema multiforme, and why does it matter?
opts: It shows intercellular immunoglobulin G throughout the epidermis, confirming the diagnosis
That pattern indicates pemphigus.
It is negative, which distinguishes erythema multiforme from pemphigoid and pemphigus
Correct. Biopsy shows interface dermatitis with vacuolar degeneration of the basal layer and necrotic keratinocytes.
It shows granular immunoglobulin A in the dermal papillae, confirming the diagnosis
That finding is the gold standard for dermatitis herpetiformis instead.
It shows linear immunoglobulin G at the basement membrane zone, confirming the diagnosis
That pattern indicates bullous pemphigoid.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which features suggest malignant rather than benign acanthosis nigricans?
opts: Gradual onset over years confined to the posterior neck and axillae
That is the pattern of the common insulin-resistant form.
Velvety hyperpigmented plaques appearing only in the inframammary folds
Fold involvement is typical of the benign form.
Lesions that wipe away completely with an isopropyl alcohol swab
That describes terra firma-forme dermatosis, a differential.
Rapid onset, extensive involvement, oral mucosal change and tripe palms
Correct — malignant disease is paraneoplastic, especially with gastric adenocarcinoma.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is field cancerisation, and how does it change management?
opts: Clinically normal skin around the lesions harbours subclinical mutations, so multiple or confluent lesions need field-directed therapy
Correct — 5-fluorouracil, imiquimod, tirbanibulin or diclofenac treat the field rather than single lesions.
Lesions spread outward from a single origin, so wide excision is required
That is not what the term describes.
Lesions seed distant sites through lymphatics, so staging is required
Actinic keratosis is an intraepidermal dysplasia, not a metastasising process.
Lesions recur at exactly the same site after treatment, so repeat cryotherapy at regular intervals is the appropriate response
Cryotherapy is lesion-directed; the field concept concerns surrounding skin.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which molecular event is critical in actinic keratosis?
opts: Loss of keratinocyte adhesion through autoantibody binding
That mechanism produces pemphigus.
Reduced filaggrin production impairing the epidermal barrier
That defect underlies atopic dermatitis.
Ultraviolet-induced mutation of TP53
Correct, and the surrounding normal-looking skin harbours subclinical mutations, called field cancerisation.
Overactivation of the hedgehog signalling pathway
That pathway is implicated in basal cell carcinoma.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is beremagene geperpavec?
opts: A non-adherent biological dressing designed for fragile skin
Mepitel and Mepilex are the dressings described; this is a gene therapy.
A topical gene therapy gel approved in 2023 for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa
Correct, accessible through dermatology referral centres and gene therapy trials.
A monoclonal antibody given intravenously for junctional epidermolysis bullosa
It is a topical gene therapy rather than an antibody.
An oral small molecule that restores keratin 5 and 14 function
It is a topical gel and does not act on keratin genes.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is first-line treatment for urticaria?
opts: Second-generation antihistamines such as cetirizine, loratadine or fexofenadine
Correct, and in chronic disease these can be scheduled at up to four times the standard dose.
A short course of oral prednisone at 40 to 60 mg for five days
That is reserved for severe acute urticaria rather than used first line.
Omalizumab given as 300 mg subcutaneously every four weeks
Omalizumab is approved for refractory chronic urticaria.
Cyclosporine titrated to response with monitoring of renal function
Cyclosporine is reserved for refractory autoimmune urticaria.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which intervention is described as the single most evidence-supported for photoaging?
opts: Ablative laser resurfacing performed every few years
Laser resurfacing is most effective for rhytids and texture but is not the top-evidence intervention.
Daily topical vitamin C at 10 to 20% concentration
This is an adjunct antioxidant.
Chemical peeling with glycolic or trichloroacetic acid
Peels provide exfoliation and remodelling rather than the strongest evidence base.
Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen at SPF 30 or above
Correct, for both preventing and slowing progression, and beginning in childhood gives maximal lifetime benefit.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the most common infectious trigger of erythema nodosum?
opts: Mycoplasma pneumoniae
Mycoplasma is a leading trigger of erythema multiforme rather than erythema nodosum.
Herpes simplex virus
Herpes simplex triggers over half of erythema multiforme cases.
Staphylococcus aureus
This organism is not among the named triggers.
Group A Streptococcus
Correct, alongside Yersinia, tuberculosis, coccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis and hepatitis B and C.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which laboratory tests evaluate the commonest cause of acanthosis nigricans?
opts: Fasting glucose, haemoglobin A1c, fasting insulin and HOMA-IR
Correct — these assess insulin resistance, with a lipid panel and body measurements for metabolic syndrome.
Serum protein electrophoresis with antinuclear and antineutrophil antibodies
That panel screens for the associations of pyoderma gangrenosum.
Antistreptolysin O titre, chest radiograph and interferon gamma release assay
That panel investigates the triggers of erythema nodosum.
Serum tryptase, complement C4 and C1-esterase inhibitor function
That panel investigates urticaria and angio-oedema.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which rosacea complication requires urgent ophthalmology referral?
opts: Papules and pustules spreading beyond the central face
This warrants dermatology input rather than urgent ophthalmology.
Ocular rosacea with keratitis, visual symptoms or corneal involvement
Correct — untreated ocular disease risks corneal scarring.
Rhinophyma causing nasal airway narrowing over several years
This is managed by dermatologic or plastic surgery rather than urgently.
Persistent central facial erythema unresponsive to topical therapy
This is treated with laser or light therapy rather than urgent referral.
